files.purpose: Owns the single hover popover that appears when the pointer rests on a Hydra head mention (a helper-agent persona name/glyph chip) inside a chat paragraph. It debounces the show by 250 ms, measures a fixed 300 pt wide SwiftUI card (glyph, persona name, task text, status line) and presents it in an application-defined NSPopover with `popover.show(relativeTo: rect, of: view, preferredEdge: .maxY)` against the mention's rect (the source fixes only the edge .maxY; which side of the mention that is on screen depends on the anchor view's coordinate flipping, see unresolved_questions); hide cancels the pending show and closes it. The card's status line tells the user whether the head is working or finished, and that a click opens its chat.

feature_notes: show(): if popover.isShown and shownID == target.threadID, returns immediately (no re-show for the same head). This early return (line 20 `if popover.isShown, shownID == target.threadID { return }`) comes before `pending?.cancel()` (line 21), so it does not cancel a pending show for another head: with A shown, show(B) starts a B task; a show(A) within 250 ms returns early, B's task survives, and when it fires it closes A (`if self.popover.isShown { self.popover.close() }`) and shows B's card anchored to B's rect. In the MarkdownView.swift:1170-1181 hover caller, any hover sample over non-head text between the two mentions calls `HydraHeadHoverPopover.shared.hide()`, which cancels the pending task, so the stale show happens only when the hover samples jump from one mention to the other and back without landing between them.

setFixedContent (UI/Chrome/Popovers.swift:29-40) frames the card to the measured size with alignment .top and .clipped(), and the hosting controller has sizingOptions = [] with contentSize = size, so a card taller than measured loses its bottom (the status line) and never its header; the source comment reads "content that turns out taller than measured loses its tail behind the panel's edge, never its header".
show(): cancels any pending task, then starts a Task that sleeps 250 ms; if self is gone or the task was cancelled, it does nothing.

After the delay: closes an already-shown popover, builds HydraHeadHoverCard, measures NSHostingView(rootView: content.frame(width: 300)).intrinsicContentSize, forces width >= 300 and height 78 when height <= 0, calls popover.setFixedContent(content, size: size), sets shownID = target.threadID, then popover.show(relativeTo: rect, of: view, preferredEdge: .maxY).
Comment explains the width pin: asked for intrinsic size unpinned, the hosting view could answer narrower than the card's fixed frame and the popover wrapped the task a couple of words per line.
hide(): cancels and nils pending, performClose(nil) if shown, sets shownID = nil. popoverDidClose also sets shownID = nil.
Name uses persona.color (SwiftUI Color); task text is limited to 3 lines.

B1->B2: only the three card fonts changed from fixed point sizes to semantic text styles: persona name .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.body, weight: .semibold); task .system(size: 12) -> .system(.callout); status .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline). On macOS those styles are nominally 13/12/11 pt, so default rendering is expected to match, but the text now follows the system text-style scale. No logic, string or geometry changes.
unresolved_questions: Exact point sizes that .body/.callout/.subheadline resolve to on the owner's macOS (expected 13/12/11) should be confirmed from Apple's macOS text-style table before hard-coding them on Windows.

Whether preferredEdge .maxY places the popover above or below the mention depends on the caller's view flipping (LinkTextView is an NSTextView, which is flipped, so likely below); the caller is outside this file.

files.purpose: Renders a chat Markdown paragraph that contains links as a selectable, non-editable AppKit NSTextView (LinkTextView) wrapped in an NSViewRepresentable, so links get click-to-open and a link popover while prose stays selectable. It rebuilds an NSAttributedString from RichLink's pretty AttributedString with cached fonts per point size, favicon attachments before links, and Hydra persona mentions rendered as a tinted dragon glyph plus a bold coloured name that can carry a custom .hydraHead attribute for hover popover and click-to-open-chat. The text view measures its own height for a proposed width, avoids per-view tracking areas for scroll performance, and defines the MergeRequestTarget environment value used by the link popover's Merge row.

attributed(): iterates RichLink.prettyAttributed runs, skipping empty strings. Font choice: .code intent -> mono (overrides others); otherwise .emphasized -> italic, then .stronglyEmphasized -> bold (bold wins when both). Link runs get [.font, .link: url]; non-link runs go through appendProse.

appendProse: with no mentions appends the string with font and colour. Otherwise personas are sorted by name length descending and scanned at each character index with hasPrefix; a match requires the character before (if any) and the character after the name (if any) to be neither letter nor number. On a hit, preceding text is flushed, a dragon attachment is appended (with .hydraHead: target.url applied to the attachment when targets[persona.name] exists), then a space in base font, then the bold coloured name (also carrying .hydraHead when there is a target). Comment: a custom attribute, not .link, so linkTextAttributes do not recolour the name in the accent. The .hydraHead value is `target.url`, defined at Core/Models/Hydra.swift:443-445 as `static let scheme = "droppycode-head"` and `var url: URL { URL(string: "\(Self.scheme)://\(threadID.uuidString)") ?? URL(fileURLWithPath: "/") }`, i.e. `droppycode-head://<threadID.uuidString>`; HydraMentionTarget.threadID(in:) (lines 447-449) reads it back only when url.scheme == "droppycode-head" and the host parses as a UUID.
dragonImage cache key: persona.asset + "@" + String(format: "%06X", persona.hex) + "@\(size)"; draws NSImage(named: persona.asset) with .sourceOver then fills with the tint using .sourceAtop.
hydraHead attribute key raw value: "droppycode.hydraHead".

MergeRequestTarget equality compares chatID only; its doc comment is truncated mid-sentence in source (ends "Compared by the"). A chat that can spawn a merge helper sets it; a link's popover then offers "Merge" at the top.

LinkTextView.init builds its own NSTextStorage -> NSLayoutManager -> NSTextContainer chain because init(frame:textContainer:) holds the container weakly and a bare container would be released, leaving every link paragraph blank. minSize .zero, maxSize greatestFiniteMagnitude both ways.

headMention / linkAndRange: glyph under point must be < numberOfGlyphs and its one-glyph bounding rect must contain the point; attribute is looked up with longestEffectiveRange over the whole storage; value may be URL or String (parsed with URL(string:)).

headMentionRect: names the run by stripping U+FFFC and trimming; if the hovered run is the glyph attachment (empty name), steps forward past non-.hydraHead characters (the space) to the next .hydraHead run and uses that as the name run; returns nil if none or empty. Rect is the bounding rect of the name glyphs, or a 1x1 rect at the point when empty.

hitTest: `guard passesProseThrough, let superview else { return super.hitTest(point) }`, so when prose is not passed through (or there is no superview) the view hit-tests normally. When passesProseThrough is true it converts the point from the superview and returns super.hitTest only over a `.link` run or a `.hydraHead` run (line 440); over anything else, including prose and favicon attachments, it returns nil so SwiftUI's whole-reply drag selection receives the event.
mouseDown over a head mention calls onOpenHead(url) and returns without selecting; otherwise super.mouseDown (which reaches clickedOnLink).

rightMouseDown and menu(for:) both call presentLinkPopover; if a link is under the point it shows LinkPopover.shared.show(url:, mergeTarget:, relativeTo: rect of the link glyphs (or 1x1 at point), of: self) and suppresses the system menu (menu returns nil).

render(): linkTextAttributes re-set each render so a theme change recolours links on screen; storage replaced only if !isEqual(to:), which also resets lastMeasuredHeight and measuredWidth to 0; always invalidateIntrinsicContentSize().

height(forWidth:): returns 0 for width <= 0 or missing layout objects; returns cached measuredHeight if width == measuredWidth; else sets container size to (width, greatest), ensureLayout, height = ceil(usedRect.height), caches it.
intrinsicContentSize: width = bounds.width if > 0 else lastLaidOutWidth; no intrinsic metric if width <= 0; otherwise (noIntrinsicMetric, height(forWidth: width)).

layout(): pins container width to bounds.width when it differs; during window live resize sets needsSettleAfterResize and returns; otherwise re-measures only when width changed by > 0.5 and invalidates intrinsic size only when height changed by > 0.5. viewDidEndLiveResize (lines 539-548): only if needsSettleAfterResize, clears it, sets `lastLaidOutWidth = bounds.width` unconditionally (no width-change threshold and no `width > 0` guard), measures height(forWidth: bounds.width) (which returns 0 for width <= 0) and invalidates the intrinsic size only when `abs(height - lastMeasuredHeight) > 0.5`.

files.purpose: Resolves bare YouTube links in chat to the video's own title so a link reads as the title instead of "youtube.com/watch". It extracts a video id from the known YouTube host and path forms, fetches the title once per id from YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint (no key), and keeps answers in a Mutex-guarded store that can be read off the main actor when RichLink builds a paragraph for the cache. Failed or empty answers are remembered as claimed so the same video is never asked twice.

files.purpose: Defines the block-level Markdown model (headings, paragraphs, fenced code, ordered/unordered/task lists, nested quotes, pipe tables, rules) and a hand-written line-based parser for agent output; inline styling is left to AttributedString. It supports incremental re-parsing for streaming replies: a Parse records how many leading blocks are stable and the UTF-8 offset to restart from, so a text that only grew by appending reuses those blocks and parses just the tail. Recursion for quotes and list children is capped at depth 8.

Foundation CharacterSet.whitespaces (spaces and tabs, including Unicode spaces, not newlines) for trimming
feature_notes: Line splitting: splits UTF-8 on 0x0A keeping empty pieces, drops one trailing 0x0D per line, records each line's UTF-8 start offset.

Stability: after parsing, stable = index of the last top-level block whose start line <= lines.count - 3 (i.e. at least two lines above the last line); restart = UTF-8 offset of that block's start line. If none, stable = 0, restart = 0. Blocks before index `stable` are reusable.

parse(_:extending:): reuses only when previous exists, previous.parse.stable > 0, the new text is strictly longer in UTF-8 and starts with the previous text's UTF-8; then parses from byte offset restart and returns previous.blocks[..<stable] + tail.blocks, stable = previous.stable + tail.stable, restart = restart + tail.restart. Otherwise a full parse.

Main loop precedence per non-blank line (trimmed with the fast trimmed()): blank flushes paragraph; fence (``` or ~~~ prefix, marker = the full run of that character) -> code block until a line whose trimmed form hasPrefix(fence) and consists only of the fence character (unterminated fence runs to end); language = text after the fence trimmed of whitespace, nil if empty; code lines kept untrimmed and joined with \n.

Heading: 1 to 6 leading '#' followed by end of line or a space; content = drop leading '#', trim whitespace, then trim characters '#' and ' ' from both ends (line 125 `content.trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "# "))`). Outcomes: a trailing '#' that belongs to the text is lost ("# Learn C#" gives text "Learn C"); a bare "#" gives .heading(level: 1, text: ""); headingLevel (line 311) accepts only `rest.isEmpty || rest.hasPrefix(" ")`, so "#\tTitle" (tab after the hashes) and "#hashtag" are not headings.

Rule: first byte '-' (0x2D), '*' (0x2A) or '_' (0x5F); every byte is that one or a space (0x20); count >= 3. In the main loop (parse) it is checked before lists, so a top-level "- - -" is a rule. parseList never calls isRule: inside an unordered list, "- - -" at indent <= first.indent matches listMarker and starts a new item with text "- -" ("* * *" likewise gives "* *"); inside an ordered list the unordered marker fails `guard marker.ordered == first.ordered else { break }`, the list ends and the main loop makes the line a rule; indented deeper than the first marker it goes to childLines and becomes a .rule child when the children are parsed. A spaceless "---"/"***"/"___" is not a list marker, so right after a list item with no child lines it is taken as a lazy continuation line and appended to the item text (line 253-254), not a rule.
Quote: trimmed line starts with '>' and depth < 8; consumes consecutive '>' lines, drops the '>' and one following space, parses the inner lines recursively at depth + 1. No lazy continuation.

Table: needs a following line, the current trimmed line contains '|', and the next line is a delimiter (contains '-' and only characters '|', ':', '-', ' '). Header from tableCells; rows continue while trimmed line is non-empty and contains '|'. tableCells strips one leading and one trailing '|', splits on '|' keeping empties, trims whitespace per cell. Column alignment markers are not recorded. isTableDelimiter (lines 325-329) requires only `trimmed.contains("-")` and every character in "|:- ", so a pipe-less "---" or "- - -" counts as a delimiter: a line containing '|' followed by "---" becomes a table header (with no rows or with the following '|' lines as rows), not a paragraph followed by a rule, whenever that '|' line was not already taken by the earlier fence, heading, rule or quote checks. The table check (line 154) runs before the list check (line 170), so "- a | b" followed by "---" is a table with header ["- a", "b"]. Rows (lines 160-165) are `tableCells(candidate)` as split and are not padded or truncated to the header's cell count; the delimiter line's cells are never counted.
List start: depth < 8 and listMarker(line) != nil and (paragraph empty, or unordered, or ordered with start == 1), so an ordered item other than 1 cannot interrupt a paragraph.

listMarker: indent = spaces count 1, tab counts 4; then `let body = line.dropFirst(indent)` (line 274) drops that many Characters, so each leading tab over-drops 3 characters: for "\t- item" indentation is 4, dropFirst(4) removes "\t- i" leaving "tem", and listMarker returns nil, so tab-indented bullets are never list markers (a top-level one is paragraph text). Inside parseList, "- parent\n\t- child" takes the indented branch (indentation 4 > 0) and, with no child lines yet and no marker, appends the trimmed text "- child" to the parent item's text instead of creating a nested list (with child lines already present it would append `line.dropFirst(min(4, contentOffset 2))` = " child" to childLines). A port must reproduce this tab-weighted character drop.unordered markers '-', '*', '+' must be followed by space or tab, content after skipping spaces/tabs, contentOffset = indent + 2, start 1. Ordered: 1 to 9 digits, then '.' or ')', then a space or end of line; content after skipping spaces; start = Int(digits) ?? 1; contentOffset = indent + digits.count + 2.

parseList: blank line continues the list if the next line is indented more than the first marker and non-blank (adds an empty child line), or if the next line is a marker with the same indent and same ordered flag (loose list); else ends. A marker with indent <= first indent starts a new item only if its ordered flag matches, else ends the list. Lines indented more than the first marker: if no child lines yet, not a marker and not a fence, the trimmed line is appended to the item text; otherwise the line (dropping min(indentation, contentOffset) characters) goes to child lines. Unindented lazy continuation lines are appended to the item text when no child lines yet and the line is not a heading, fence or quote; otherwise the list ends.
Task items: item text trimmed of whitespace; prefix "[ ] " -> checked false; lowercased prefix "[x] " -> checked true; the 4 characters are removed. Children are parsed recursively at depth + 1.
parseList fallback: if the start line has no marker, returns .paragraph(line) and start + 1.
trimmed(line) fast path: returns the line unchanged when its first and last UTF-8 bytes are both in 0x21...0x7E; otherwise trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).

Paragraph: consecutive non-block lines are stored untrimmed (line 180 `paragraph.append(line)`, not `trimmed`), joined with \n and only the joined text is trimmed of whitespace and newlines at its two ends (line 87 `.trimmed`), so continuation lines keep their leading indentation (and inner lines their trailing spaces) inside the .paragraph string;empty results are dropped; paragraph start line recorded for stability.

B1->B2: one line changed in flushParagraph: paragraph.joined(separator: "\n").trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) became .trimmed, the project extension that is defined as the same call, so parsing behaviour is unchanged.
unresolved_questions: Setext headings, indented code blocks, HTML blocks and lazy quote continuation are not supported by this parser; a port must reproduce these omissions rather than use a CommonMark library to keep parity.
In parseList the restart offset semantics for nested list children are not tracked (only top-level blockLines), which is by design but worth mirroring exactly.
